claims.text: A defect-aware data-driven approach will predict electrical conductivity in bulk HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than traditional defect-free analytical models.
The accuracy advantage will apply in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
The relevant bulk cast HfNbTaTiZr contains inherent microstructural defects.
The relevant HfNbTaTiZr specimen contains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed framework combines machine learning, first-principles corrections for defect-induced scattering, and temperature-dependent transport models.
The conductivity evaluation will cover 0–200 K and 300–1200 K on samples verified to contain about 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen interstitials act as defect sites in the alloy.
Oxygen interstitials alter electrical conduction pathways.
Accounting for oxygen-related defect scattering and temperature-dependent electron-phonon interactions corrects the over-idealized conduction pathways of perfect-crystal predictions.
These corrections lead to more representative conductivity forecasts.
Traditional analytical models have conductivity errors of approximately 25–40%.
The proposed model will reduce conductivity error to below approximately 10–15% in both temperature regimes.
Existing analytical predictions assume ideal, defect-free crystal structures.
Neglecting defect-induced scattering causes significant deviations between analytical predictions and measurements.
The proposed approach is applicable only to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with defect profiles similar to samples containing around 1 wt.% oxygen.
The approach may not generalize to substantially different impurity levels or processing histories.
The contribution of oxygen-induced scattering to electron mobility has not been fully quantified.

The model is falsified if it fails to achieve a statistically significant reduction in prediction error, operationalized as at least a 10% improvement over traditional predictions across both regimes.
